newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dairy Farm says fresh funds for Franklins.
newsitem.headline: Dairy Farm says fresh funds for Franklins.

text.p: Retailer Dairy Farm International Holdings Ltd will inject US$80-90 million a year over the next four years into Franklins, its troubled Australian supermarket chain, Singapore's Business Times said on Friday.
It quoted Chris Nelson, Dairy Farm's chief executive officer, as saying the money would be spent converting 120 basic non-perishable goods stores into more profitable fresh food shops.
By 2000, there would only be 50 Franklins No Frills stores left from 194 last year, he said. But the changes would not contribute to the bottom line for another 18 to 24 months, he said.

In its 1996 results announcement on Tuesday, Dairy Farm said it spent US$77.5 million on repositioning provisions for Franklins and its Kwik Save Plc operation in Britain, which dragged its net attributable profit down by 76 percent to US$27.9 million.
The Business Times quoted Finance director Edouard Ettedgui as saying the company had no plans to sell its interest in Kwik Save.
The group planned to open two or three "hypermarkets" in Taiwan to compete against such stores which had been eating into the share of neighbourhood supermarkets, the newspaper said.
French hypermarket operator Casino would manage the hypermarkets in Taipei with the first due to start in 1998, it said.
Dairy Farm is 52-percent owned by Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd, a holding company for Asian conglomerate Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd.
